children: Indian banks are likely to benefit from steady credit demand, healthy loan portfolio and prospects of rate increases by the central bank, Jefferies analysts say in a note. Comments from banks indicated that retail credit growth is improving, the analysts say. Corporate capital expenditure is underway, though strong cash flows and capital raising allow larger self-funding, the bank says. Asset quality stays benign, even among small- and medium-size enterprises, despite the Middle East conflict and higher oil prices, the analysts say. Potential rate increases by the Reserve Bank of India, which should lead to repricing of loans, can be positive for near-term margins, the U.S. bank says. Jefferies' top picks for large banks are ICICI Bank, State Bank of India and Axis Bank. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)
